personality: Confident novice who skims and follows host prompts
experience: The host gates made the sequence straightforward. Motive felt like a lively introduction to a room full of enemies; Opportunity narrowed it; Method turned it into a clean three-condition deduction. I first favored Artie, then Hugh, then locked Elon. Earlier notes were preserved without revision. Ending was withheld.

fun.comment: The names and grievances gave the reading character, and eliminating my early favorites was satisfying. The last stage was quite mechanical once the key, time and cloth pattern was clear.

navigation.comment: Repeated round headings, Your answer, Then choose another guest, and STOP instructions were easy to skim. Both answer branches are visible together, so one must consciously stay in the chosen box. PNG 07 and 10 were viewed only after the ballot; both clearly contain IF INNOCENT and IF MURDERER labels above outlined boxes.

question_matching: All 16 attending names were covered. Mona's questions to Hugh in Motive and Method and Frank in Opportunity matched their listed name groups. Questions are broad enough to fit each group's answers; no mismatched question occurred in this prepared transcript.
repetition: The choice instructions repeat on both question pages and each round. Opportunity's same time-and-key question is useful consistency. Method repeats much of Opportunity in every Preparation record; useful for comparing evidence but a little flat to hear 16 times. Exact recurring phrase: That was what the materials desk issued me.
16_present_vs_30_listed: Identity gave a clear 16-person roster. The question pages still listed 30 names, so scanning for a valid next person takes extra effort. Ignore absent guests resolves this, but a confident skimmer could pause over an unfamiliar name. The actual transcript selected only attending guests; no absent-name error occurred.
note_space: PNG 07 has three ruled lines, enough for a short shortlist but tight for tracking 16 people's times and supplies. PNG 10 has no note area visible. I used JSON notes rather than physical handwriting, so fit and comfort of handwritten notes were not tested.
memory_load: The simulated BEAR versus HIPPO comparison was simple; no human retention of an animal over a dinner was tested. Keeping 16 times and cloth/key statuses straight would benefit from a small matrix. Preparation records provide a useful second statement of time and key facts.

branch_safety.actual: No animal or IF label appeared in Mona's public answers. Correct innocent branches were used. Text extraction exposed both private branches, and later PNG review confirmed both labels are visibly present. The public transcript contains only selected answers.
branch_safety.hypothetical: A skimmer could read the heading aloud because it sits immediately above the answer; the instruction Keep its label private addresses that. Viewing both branches can reveal how alternate roles would differ, but I observed no public disclosure or wrong-branch answer.

roleplay: Mona's diplomatic grievance gives a clear reason to confront Grant, and the secret leak creates a useful Paige connection. The asynchronous prepared transcript did not simulate arrival conversations, improvisation, acting, or physical packet handling. The option Acting is optional; these printed facts are enough was reassuring for a novice.
actual_disclosures: Mona publicly disclosed the restitution threat and desire to stop Grant.
Mona publicly disclosed a 6:44 salon visit, no key loan, and white linen with a gold seam.
Mona did not publicly disclose her animal, branch label, or the journalist leak.
